subject: Mathematics

source.authority: KICD Grade 4 Mathematics regular curriculum revised 2024

scope: Eight suggested lessons for Addition 1.2 and eight for Subtraction 1.3. This is a proposed original teaching sequence, not an approved timetable or KICD-mandated lesson-by-lesson schedule.
copyright: All learner-facing words and examples are newly authored, not reproductions of KICD text.

lessons.title: Why one regrouping works
lessons.goal: Explain a ten-for-one exchange in the ones column.
lessons.priorLearning: Check place-value alignment and learner's ability to explain the necessary number representation.

model.why: 3 ones plus 8 ones make 11: exchange 10 ones for one ten and write the remaining one.

guidedActivity: Build 11 counters in ones; circle 10 and exchange for a tens card.
Add the other columns, naming each place.

exitCheck.reason: 15 ones become 5 ones and one carried ten.

lessons.misconceptionRepair: Forgetting the carried ten: point to the new ten before adding tens.
lessons.teacherPrompt: Ask the learner why the number of objects does not change during exchanging.

delivery.lowCost: Use paper and a drawn four-column chart or locally available counters; allow spoken explanation.
delivery.accessibility: Readable numeric columns, labels and non-colour-only visual grouping.
delivery.assessmentStatus: editorial self-check only, not a stored examination or mastery event

lessons.title: One regrouping in context
lessons.goal: Solve a real four-digit sum with exactly one exchange.
lessons.priorLearning: Check place-value alignment and learner's ability to explain the necessary number representation.

model.why: 6+7=13 ones; write 3 ones and add one ten to the next column.

guidedActivity: Read a two-day collection story and underline the two amounts.
Explain the carried ten in words and check using subtraction.

exitCheck.reason: 13 ones make one ten and three ones.

lessons.misconceptionRepair: Misaligned digits: label thousands/hundreds/tens/ones before calculating.
lessons.teacherPrompt: Ask for an estimate and inverse check.

lessons.title: Two exchanges in neighbouring columns
lessons.goal: Show two distinct base-ten exchanges in one addition.
lessons.priorLearning: Check place-value alignment and learner's ability to explain the necessary number representation.

model.why: 15 ones require carrying one ten; the tens then total 12 and require carrying one hundred.

guidedActivity: Draw 15 ones and exchange ten for a ten card.
Draw 12 tens and exchange ten for one hundred.

exitCheck.reason: 13 ones and 11 tens produce two exchanges.

lessons.misconceptionRepair: Only one carry shown: circle each column where the total exceeds nine.
lessons.teacherPrompt: Ask the learner to show both exchanges with separate arrows.

lessons.title: Two exchanges starting beyond ones
lessons.goal: Regroup in tens and hundreds even when ones do not need exchanging.
lessons.priorLearning: Check place-value alignment and learner's ability to explain the necessary number representation.
guidedActivity: Work in four columns and mark each exchange.
Compare two-exchange examples where ones do and do not carry.
lessons.misconceptionRepair: Assuming all carries begin at ones: check each column independently.
lessons.teacherPrompt: Ask what causes an exchange in hundreds.

lessons.title: Nearest-ten estimate of a sum
lessons.priorLearning: Check place-value alignment and learner's ability to explain the necessary number representation.

model.why: 2,463 rounds down to 2,460 while 1,328 rounds up to 1,330; add to estimate 3,790.

guidedActivity: Mark each addend on a line between neighbouring tens.
Calculate both estimated and exact sums and compare.
lessons.misconceptionRepair: Confusing estimate with exact answer: label both outcomes.
lessons.teacherPrompt: Ask whether the estimate is close enough to detect a place-value mistake.

lessons.title: Patterns with a repeated addition step
lessons.goal: Continue a four-digit pattern using a constant positive difference.
lessons.priorLearning: Check place-value alignment and learner's ability to explain the necessary number representation.

model.why: Each term is the previous term plus exactly 125; checking neighbours confirms the rule.

guidedActivity: Use five number cards to create +125 sequence.
Ask another learner to identify the rule by subtraction.
lessons.misconceptionRepair: Increasing the step itself: display four equal +125 arrows.
lessons.teacherPrompt: Ask how subtracting neighbours verifies an addition pattern.

lessons.title: Invent and verify an addition pattern
lessons.goal: Create your own pattern with a sum below 10,000.
lessons.priorLearning: Check place-value alignment and learner's ability to explain the necessary number representation.

model.why: A repeatable rule adds 175; each difference is 175.

guidedActivity: Write a pattern and hide the rule.
Swap with a partner to solve and explain using subtraction.
lessons.misconceptionRepair: Making a new rule at each step: verify differences.
lessons.teacherPrompt: Ask the learner for two different starting values that share one step.

lessons.title: Choose addition for real quantities
lessons.goal: Solve a local context problem and justify using addition.
lessons.priorLearning: Check place-value alignment and learner's ability to explain the necessary number representation.

model.why: The story combines two quantities of the same units, so their sum gives the total packets.

guidedActivity: Write a two-term school-garden collection story.
Solve and label units, then estimate for reasonableness.

exitCheck.reason: Two book quantities combine into 5,085 books.

lessons.misconceptionRepair: Adding unlike units: identify matching quantities first.
lessons.teacherPrompt: Ask what story wording would instead require subtraction.

lessons.title: Subtract with no exchanging
lessons.goal: Subtract aligned four-digit numbers when no top digit is smaller.
lessons.priorLearning: Check place-value alignment and learner's ability to explain the necessary number representation.

model.why: Every column has enough units; subtract like units directly.

guidedActivity: Build a place-value table for 7,864 and 2,532.
Subtract ones to thousands and check by addition.

exitCheck.reason: Every top digit is at least its matching bottom digit.

lessons.misconceptionRepair: Subtracting a larger place from a smaller one: align labels.
lessons.teacherPrompt: Ask how adding the difference to the amount removed checks the answer.

lessons.title: Use subtraction to find a remainder
lessons.goal: Translate a situation into no-regroup subtraction.
lessons.priorLearning: Check place-value alignment and learner's ability to explain the necessary number representation.

model.why: Finding what is left means subtracting the amount removed from the starting quantity.

guidedActivity: Invent a library-book remainder story using 9,754 and 4,321.
Write units and verify with inverse addition.
lessons.misconceptionRepair: Reversing starting and removed quantities: label the starting stock.
lessons.teacherPrompt: Ask which quantity is the whole and which part was removed.

lessons.title: Exchange through zeros
lessons.goal: Explain subtraction when zeros block an immediate exchange.
lessons.priorLearning: Check place-value alignment and learner's ability to explain the necessary number representation.

model.why: Exchange one thousand for ten hundreds, then one hundred for ten tens and one ten for ten ones; the original total stays 5,004.

guidedActivity: Draw five thousands and four ones.
Trace each exchange through zeros; write 4 thousands, 9 hundreds, 9 tens and 14 ones before subtracting.

exitCheck.reason: Exchange through the zero tens; check 4,737+2,468=7,205.

lessons.misconceptionRepair: Writing tens as ten without decreasing the borrowed-from column: trace each exchange.
lessons.teacherPrompt: Ask why 5,004 can also be represented by 4 thousands, 9 hundreds, 9 tens and 14 ones.

lessons.title: Regroup in real quantities
lessons.goal: Subtract four-digit quantities after exchanging and check the result.
lessons.priorLearning: Check place-value alignment and learner's ability to explain the necessary number representation.

model.why: Use place-value exchanges to make enough units for subtraction; inverse addition confirms 4,329+3,675=8,004.

guidedActivity: Represent 8,004 on paper in thousands, hundreds, tens and ones.
Write and justify each exchange before finding the difference.
lessons.misconceptionRepair: Forgetting to subtract from the original higher column after an exchange: mark traded units.
lessons.teacherPrompt: Ask the learner to prove the answer using addition.

lessons.title: Estimate a difference
lessons.goal: Round each number independently to the nearest ten before subtracting.
lessons.priorLearning: Check place-value alignment and learner's ability to explain the necessary number representation.

model.why: 6,457 rounds to 6,460 and 2,384 rounds to 2,380, producing an estimated difference of 4,080.

guidedActivity: Locate each number between its neighbouring tens.
Write estimated difference and exact difference separately.
lessons.misconceptionRepair: Rounding the exact final result instead of both operands: name the procedure.
lessons.teacherPrompt: Ask how far the estimate differs from the exact answer.

lessons.title: Subtraction patterns
lessons.goal: Continue a decreasing pattern with a fixed step.
lessons.priorLearning: Check place-value alignment and learner's ability to explain the necessary number representation.

model.why: Subtract 250 each time; equal differences confirm a consistent rule.

guidedActivity: Create number cards 8,500 to 7,500.
Arrange cards and label the −250 jumps.
lessons.misconceptionRepair: Changing step size: compare each pair by subtraction.
lessons.teacherPrompt: Ask what the same pattern looks like on a number line.

lessons.title: Remainders in everyday tasks
lessons.goal: Identify the remainder after part of a stock is distributed.
lessons.priorLearning: Check place-value alignment and learner's ability to explain the necessary number representation.

model.why: Start with 7,600 cards and remove 2,350; 5,250 remain, checked because 5,250+2,350=7,600.

guidedActivity: Tell a school stock story and write what remains.
Calculate the answer, label units and use inverse addition.
lessons.misconceptionRepair: Adding when the question asks how many remain: draw part-whole bar.
lessons.teacherPrompt: Ask the learner to compare remainder and difference scenarios.

lessons.title: Comparing quantities using subtraction
lessons.goal: Explain how subtraction finds the difference between two comparable counts.
lessons.priorLearning: Check place-value alignment and learner's ability to explain the necessary number representation.

model.why: Two book collections share units, and the difference 8,540−3,125=5,415 shows how many more the larger collection has.

guidedActivity: Compare two labelled school book counts using a bar model.
Explain the answer as '5,415 more exercise books' rather than remaining stock.

exitCheck.reason: The larger group exceeds the smaller by 5,225 items.

lessons.misconceptionRepair: Confusing comparison with take-away: both subtract but the words 'more than' describe a difference.
lessons.teacherPrompt: Ask which quantity is larger and what comparison tells us.
